description: A modular, stack-agnostic toolkit for AI coding agents to autonomously find, reproduce, and patch vulnerabilities.

written.description: Reads a codebase and its commit history, builds a threat model from them, and sends agents to chase each hypothesis it raises. It then tries to reproduce each finding in a sandbox and attacks its own patch to check the fix holds, working from source alone with no running target.

alive.last_commit_message:
feat(ledger): backfill content coverage for campaigns that predate it

A knowledge base built before the content ledger existed holds
completed campaigns with no record of what their files contained, so
the first `--scan-mode changed` run over it cannot tell what moved and
scans the whole target once to find out. An operator who already paid
for a file-by-file pass over a large tree pays for it again.

`scripts/knowledge.py backfill-coverage` fills the ledger in after the
fact. For every completed campaign under the repository that has no
content rows, it records the identity of each file the campaign
covered, taken from the content the file had when the campaign ran:
the commit the run recorded on its artifacts, a commit the operator
names with `--at`, or the working tree with `--assume-unchanged`, in
that order of trust. Commit content is hashed from git objects, never
from the tree, so an edit made since the scan is reported as changed
by the next run. Rows from a commit carry no mtime, which makes the
ledger hash rather than trust a timestamp when it compares.

Campaigns whose content cannot be established are skipped with the
reason, campaigns that already have rows are left alone, and
`--dry-run` reports without writing. The `changed` planner's
whole-scan notice now names the command, so the operator can stop and
backfill instead.

Change-Id: If114c446ffc3529cc0a8f3c4911f3560b726034d
